newsitem.title: INDIA: India says infrastructure crunch may hit growth.
newsitem.headline: India says infrastructure crunch may hit growth.

text.p: Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said on Friday that slow growth in six key infrastructure sectors this year may affect the government's aims of achieving high economic growth.

He told parliament while replying to a debate on the federal budget for 1996/97 (April-March) that electricity, coal, steel, crude oil, refining and cement industries had grown at 4.6 percent in the first quarter, compared to 11.8 percent in the same quarter of the previous year.
"If they are like this, I am afraid we will not be abe to achieve our (growth) targets," Chidambaram said.
India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 7.0 percent in 1995/96, against an expectation of 6.2 percent. It expects the GDP to grow by 6.6 percent in 1996/97.
